title: Short Stuff: The Man Who Didn’t Eat for a Year
summary: Short Stuff episode on Angus Barbieri, a Scottish man who weighed about 456 pounds (21 stone) and went 382 days without eating solid food in a supervised, outpatient fast in Dundee, drinking only coffee, tea, sparkling water, and taking vitamins and electrolyte supplements. Doctors documented the fast in the Postgraduate Medical Journal. The hosts cover his bowel movements, blood glucose of about 30, hypercalcemia, his refeeding with a boiled egg and bread, Guinness record recognition, and the longer hunger strike record of Dennis Glor Goodwin (385 days). They close with the dangers of prolonged fasting, including heart muscle breakdown, sudden death, and refeeding syndrome.

segments.title: Introduction to Angus Barbieri
segments.summary: The hosts introduce Angus Barbieri, a man who weighed 456 pounds in Scotland and went 382 days without solid food under medical supervision, and mention the show's earlier fasting episode.

segments.title: The supervised fast and medical documentation
segments.summary: Barbieri's doctors put him on a fast. He stopped eating and went 382 days with no food, drinking coffee, tea, and sparkling water, and taking vitamins, yeast, sodium, and potassium supplements. He stayed an outpatient, kept his life going, and his doctors tested him to confirm he was not eating. The case was published in the Postgraduate Medical Journal.

segments.title: Ad break
segments.summary: Break before the answer to the teaser question about what else Barbieri did not do.

segments.title: Bowel movements during the fast
segments.summary: The hosts answer the teaser: Barbieri did not poop often, going roughly 40 to 50 days between bowel movements. What he passed was cellular debris, and he pooped about seven to nine times in the year.

segments.title: Weight loss, refeeding, and blood glucose
segments.summary: Barbieri reached about 180 pounds and regained only a little weight over the following years. He broke the fast with a boiled egg, bread with butter, and black coffee. His blood glucose was about 30, far below normal levels, and the hosts discuss how it is hard to fake that test.

segments.title: Hypercalcemia and Guinness record
segments.summary: Barbieri developed hypercalcemia. The hosts suggest his bones may have dissolved as he lost weight quickly. Guinness World Records recognized him, then stopped opening such records to others because of the danger.

segments.title: Dennis Glor Goodwin hunger strike record
segments.summary: The hosts mention Dennis Glor Goodwin, who went 385 days without eating during a hunger strike over a rape charge he said he was innocent of, before being force-fed through a tube. The hosts could not find any follow-up on his case.

segments.title: Dangers of long fasts and refeeding syndrome
segments.summary: The hosts explain that long fasts can be deadly. Once fat stores run out, the body breaks down muscle, including heart tissue, which can cause sudden death, often around six to eight weeks depending on body weight. Refeeding can also kill people through nutrient overdose. The hosts advise against long fasts.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh thanks listeners for joining the Short Stuff episode and gives the show credits.
